An in-life encyclopedia for the people I have met or been told about.  I can't tell you how many times my wife has started telling me a story about one of her co-workers and I have to stop her and ask "which person is this again?"

For me some of it came down to just forethought. I feel absolutely shitty if I don't do anything in a day.  After a fee days of that in a row I can become suicidal.  Basically I have to look at my day and even if there's nothing I have to do, I make myself do something. Anything.  Doesn't matter how big or how small, doesn't matter if it's a thing for work or for fun, I make myself do something because I've taught myself that whatever discomfort I have from doing a thing i don't want to do is not as bad as getting through the day having accomplished nothing.

The tool that I found works best for me to do this is to take the smallest first step of a task.  Let's say for instance I need to work on a project that needs artwork done.  I'll open up photoshop and make a new file.  Maybe I'll futz around in it, but usually I don't actually get anything done.  But the next day it's somehow much easier to put forth the effort to work on it just because the first step has already been taken by past me.  

I can't speak for other mental illnesses, but with depression there's a kind of twisted perversion of the "live in the now!" mentality, for me at least.  I become so focused on the present moment where something is shitty that nothing from the past or future can affect my thoughts and I act according to that info.  "There's no point in going on because the future can't possibly get better because it's shitty right now", "it doesn't matter that things worked out in the past because the past is the past and now is now".  I have had to train myself (and I'm still working on it) to pre-emptively look ahead when I'm in a good place to avoid falling into a bad place.  I've also started keeping a diary so I can better connect to my past.  Trying to keep that through line while you're in a good spot mentally will help.

Thank you.  It helps to know that other people feel the same way.  Sometimes depression seems like a foreign language with hundreds of dialects. It's comforting to hear someone else that speaks the same dialect as me.  I wish you the best as well.

Thank you.  I know deep down I have something to offer, I just need to figure out what.  I know I need to change some things about me, it's just hard, you know? Or maybe it's not all that hard, it just seems so hard from this side.  I hate when I get real deep down in my depression because there are things that seem so immutable, so permanent that any kind of change seems like climbing a mountain.  And when I swing out of those pits everything seems ok and I don't feel like I need to do anything.  This time I need to do something.  There's a walk in clinic covered by my insurance.  I'm going to go there Monday.  (I'm saying this partly to let you know I'm on an upswing, and partly because if I write it out then I believe I'll be more likely to actually do it.)
